extracted.intended_audience: President and Council of Fort St. George; senior East India Company officials and administrators in India
extracted.subtask_description: Instructions and binding policy guidance for implementing the surrender of revenue assignments, negotiating treaties, repairing public works, and administering/allocating the Nabob's revenues and debts in the Carnatic (Madras Presidency) following the 1784 Board of Control directions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rajah accountable only for government share of crop
rubrics_metrics.description: Our opinion being that the Rajah ought to be answerable for no more than the amount of what he admits was collected by his people for the government share of the crop;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proceed on principle that Rajah's liability is limited to government share actually collected. If proceedings do not clearly show inclusion of portions taken from assignees (e.g., Mr. Benfield), or if compensation status is unclear, suspend application of deposits and refer for further explanation and orders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restore grain to assignees and assist recovery of debts
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommended to him 'to restore to Mr. Benfield ... the grain of the last year ... and farther, to give Mr. Benfield all reasonable assistance in recovering such debts as should appear to have been justly due to him from the inhabitants;'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use recommendation to Rajah as means to protect assignees' rights; the manner and time of execution are left to the Rajah unless difficulties arise, in which case suspend and consult the Board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspend application of deposit if facts unclear
rubrics_metrics.description: But should any such difficulty suggest itself, you will suspend any application of the deposit, until you have fully explained the same to us, and have received our further orders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not apply the one lac of pagodas deposit until local officers have resolved whether the Rajah's admitted collections include grain taken from assignees and whether compensation has been made. If uncertain, report up for directions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rajah permitted to repair Anicut and banks by former usage
rubrics_metrics.description: It appeared to us perfectly reasonable that the Rajah should be permitted to repair those banks, and the Anicut, in the same manner as had been practised in times past; and we directed you to establish such regulations, by reference to former usage, for keeping the said banks in repair, as would be effectual, and remove all cause of complaint in future.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame regulations that formalize customary practice for repairs so they are effective and avoid future disputes; refer to prior surveys and reports (e.g., Bourchier 1764) when establishing rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek Nabob permission for materials and lease limited term
rubrics_metrics.description: If ... necessary or expedient, you apply to the Nabob, in our name, to desire that his Highness will permit proper spots of ground to be set out ... where the Rajah and his people may at all times take sand and earth sufficient for these repairs; and that his Highness will grant his lease of such spots of land for a certain term of years to the Company, at a reasonable annual rent, ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request defined parcels on the Trichinopoly side for material extraction and secure a lease for a fixed term at reasonable rent; couple such leases with safeguards for Nabob's rights and conditions on Rajah's punctual payment of dues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lease conditional on punctual payment of peshcush and rent
rubrics_metrics.description: Should you succeed in reconciling the Nabob to this measure, we think it but just that the proposed lease shall remain no longer in force than whilst the Rajah shall be punctual in the payment of the annual peshcush to the Nabob, as well as the rent to be reserved for the spots of ground.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make leases explicitly terminable if Rajah defaults on stipulated payments; use punctuality as condition precedent for continuing privileges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employ Company-appointed engineers at Rajah's expense
rubrics_metrics.description: It should be recommended ... that skilful engineers, appointed by the Company, be employed at the Rajah's expense to conduct all the necessary works, with the strictest attention to the respective rights and interests of both parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign Company engineers (under Madras government appointment) to supervise works to avoid disputes; engineers act with impartiality and provide direct redress via Madras government if either party claims injury.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediate redress via Madras government for disputes
rubrics_metrics.description: But should either party unexpectedly conceive themselves to be injured, immediate redress might be obtained by application to the government of Madras, under whose appointment the engineer will act, without any discussion between the parties ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Madras government's authority to resolve complaints quickly and avoid bilateral disputes that could disturb harmony.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surrender assignment of revenues to the Nabob without delay
rubrics_metrics.description: We have resolved that the assignment shall be surrendered; and we do accordingly direct our President ... without delay, to surrender the same to his Highness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effect immediate formal surrender of the revenue assignment to the Nabob while negotiating protective arrangements and expecting reciprocal concessions to secure Company interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nabob to give soucar security of 12 lacs pagodas per annum
rubrics_metrics.description: That ... the Nabob shall give soucar security for the punctual payment, by instalments, into the Company's treasury, of twelve lacs of pagodas per annum ... until those debts, with interest, shall be discharged;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain formal soucar security from the Nabob to ensure payment of 12 lacs per annum into Company's treasury until private and Company debts are liquidated; use instalments and monitoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reserve right to demand additional security on default
rubrics_metrics.description: we nevertheless think it our duty ... to insist on a declaration, that, in the event of the failure of the security proposed, or in default of payment at the stipulated periods, we reserve to ourselves full right to demand of the Nabob such additional security, by assignment on his country, as shall be effectual for answering the purposes of the agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include explicit contractual reservation allowing the Company to seek territorial/revenue assignments to secure payments if the Nabob defaults; make this a precondition of protection to creditors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treaty principle: joint contribution to military support
rubrics_metrics.description: one or more treaty or treaties with the Company, grounded on this principle of equity: That all the contracting parties shall be bound to contribute jointly to the support of the military force and garrisons, as well in peace as in war.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Negotiate treaties obliging Company, Nabob, and Rajah to jointly fund and support military establishments; bind contributions to specific revenues/districts to ensure punctual payments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Company to settle military peace establishment and secure payments
rubrics_metrics.description: That the military peace establishment shall be forthwith settled and adjusted by the Company ... the Nabob and Rajah must ... specify particular districts and revenues for securing the due and regular payment of their contributions into the treasury of the Company ... with power for the Company, in case of failure ... to enter upon and possess such districts ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Company to define peace establishment and require defined revenue assignments/districts as security; include power of entry/possession upon default, balanced by assurances of civil administration rights for native rulers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assurance to preserve Nabob/Rajah civil authority
rubrics_metrics.description: this part of the treaty be coupled with a most positive assurance, on our part, of our determination to support the dignity and authority of the Nabob and Rajah in the exclusive administration of the civil government and revenues of their respective countries;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When demanding security rights, explicitly guarantee that the Nabob and Rajah retain substantive civil authority over administration and revenues, to preserve legitimacy and reduce resistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggregate revenue applied to war during hostilities
rubrics_metrics.description: That the whole aggregate revenue of the contracting parties shall, during the war, be under the application of the Company, and shall continue as long after the war as shall be necessary, to discharge the burdens contracted by it;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During wartime, centralize aggregate revenues under Company control and apply them to war expenditures and contracted burdens, while specifying that this should not unduly deprive native rulers of collection authority if they faithfully perform conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Company and native powers refrain from commercial application of revenues during war
rubrics_metrics.description: that the Company, on their part, shall engage to refrain, during the war, from the application of any part of their revenues to any commercial purposes whatsoever, but apply the whole, save only the ordinary charges of their civil government, to the purposes of the war; that the Nabob and the Rajah shall in like manner engage ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bind all contracting parties by treaty to dedicate revenues to defence/war needs and not divert funds to commerce or non-essential purposes during hostilities; preserve minimal civil government charges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ascertain and protect sum necessary for civil establishment
rubrics_metrics.description: that the sum be now ascertained which is indispensably necessary to be applied to those purposes, and which is to be held sacred under every emergency, and set apart previous to the application of the rest of the revenues, as hereby stipulated, for the purposes of mutual or common defence ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define in treaty a protected civil establishment sum to be set aside before any war or defence appropriation; this prevents ambiguity and preserves essential governance functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Company to produce regular accounts of revenue application
rubrics_metrics.description: The Company are to engage, during the time they shall administer the revenues, to produce to the other contracting parties regular accounts of the application thereof to the purposes stipulated by the treaty, and faithfully apply them in support of the war.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure transparency by delivering periodic, faithful accounting of revenue expenditures to Nabob and Rajah while Company administers funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit natives' standing troops; Company to supply additional military aid if required
rubrics_metrics.description: the Nabob shall be satisfied of the propriety of avoiding all unnecessary expense, and will therefore agree not to maintain a greater number of troops than shall be necessary for the support of his dignity and the splendor of the durbar, which number shall be specified in the treaty; and if any military aid is requisite ... the Company must be bound to furnish him with such aid: the Rajah of Tanjore must likewise become bound by similar engagements, and be entitled to similar aid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fix an explicit ceiling on native ceremonial/standing forces in treaty and obligate Company to provide additional forces for revenue security or extraordinary needs; ensure parity of obligations across parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permit existing renters to hold leases subject to Nabob consent and indemnify losses
rubrics_metrics.description: we direct that you apply to the Nabob, in our name, for his consent that they may be permitted to hold their leases to the end of the stipulated term ... But if ... his Highness should be impressed with any particular aversion to comply with this proposition, we do not desire you to insist upon it as an essential part ... but, in that event, you must take especial care to give such indemnification to the renters for any loss they may sustain as you judge to be reasonable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek Nabob acceptance to honor existing lease terms; if refused, provide reasonable indemnification to affected renters rather than force the matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect faithful native officials from suffering
rubrics_metrics.description: It equally concerns the honor of our government, that such natives as may have been put in any degree of authority over the collections, in consequence of the deed of assignment, and who have proved faithful to their trust, shall not suffer inconvenience on account of their fidelity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include explicit protections for native officials who have performed faithfully under prior arrangements; do not penalize them when arrangements change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use conciliation and prudence before issuing coercive financial instruments
rubrics_metrics.description: the step of issuing the Torana Chits in Lord Macartney's own name can only be justified upon the ground of absolute necessity ... every precaution ought to have been used and more time allowed for proving that necessity, by previous acts of address, civility, and conciliation ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid issuing demands likely to offend native rulers without first exhausting conciliatory means; prioritize diplomacy and avoid acts derogatory to native authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communicate opinions about Indian powers with prudence and secrecy
rubrics_metrics.description: we earnestly recommend that those opinions and speculations be communicated to us with prudence, discretion, and all possible secrecy, and the terms in which they are conveyed be expressed in a manner as little offensive as possible to the powers whom they may concern ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reporting suspicions or assessments of Indian powers, frame them cautiously and maintain strict secrecy to avoid diplomatic offense or leaks.

rubrics_metrics.name: 1767 consolidated debt recognized at 10% interest
rubrics_metrics.description: In speaking of the loan of 1767, we are to be understood as speaking of the debt as constituted by the original bonds of that year, bearing interest at 10 l. per cent;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When accounting and distributing funds, treat the 1767 consolidated debt as fixed at 10% interest to end of 1784 unless special instructions indicate otherwise; disregard later bonds claiming higher rates without direction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cavalry Loan (1777) and 1777 consolidated debt: treatment and limits of Company sanction
rubrics_metrics.description: The loan of 1777 ... has no sanction or authority from us; ... we have resolved so far to recognize the justice of those debts as to extend to them that protection which ... we have seen cause to allow to the other two classes of debts. But ... we do not mean to debar you from receiving any complaints ... and if any complaints are offered, we order that the grounds of all such be attentively examined by you, and be transmitted to us ... for our final decision;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat the 1777 (Cavalry) loan with caution: although not sanctioned, extend conditional protection for expediency while investigating objections. Refer complaints and evidence home for final adjudication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal distribution rules for the twelve lacs of pagodas
rubrics_metrics.description: That the debt be made up in the following manner ... The debt consolidated in 1767 to be made up to the end of the year 1784, with the current interest at ten per cent. The Cavalry Loan to be made up to the same period, with the current interest at twelve per cent. The debt consolidated in 1777 to be made up to the same period, with the current interest at twelve per cent, to November, 1781, and from thence with the current interest at six per cent. The twelve lacs annually to be applied,—1. To the growing interest on the Cavalry Loan, at twelve per cent. 2. To the growing interest on the debt of 1777, at six per cent. The remainder to be equally divided: one half to be applied to the extinction of the Company's debt; the other half to be applied to the payment of growing interest at 10 l. per cent, and towards the discharge of the principal of the debt of 1767. ... When the Cavalry Loan shall be thus discharged, there shall then be paid towards the discharge of the Company's debt seven lacs. To the growing interest and capital of the 1777 loan, five lacs. When the Company's debt shall be discharged, the whole is then to be applied in discharge of the debt 1777.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the multi-stage application order exactly: pay specified interest obligations first (Cavalry then 1777), split remainder equally between Company's debt and 1767 obligations, then reallocate amounts as loans are extinguished; apply any extra Tanjore peshcush to reduce Company's debt if agreed by Nabob.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creditor acquiescence required for participation in fund
rubrics_metrics.description: we expressly order, that, if any creditor of the Nabob, a servant of the Company, or being under our protection, shall refuse to express his acquiescence in these arrangements, he shall not only be excluded from receiving any share of the fund under your distribution, but shall be prohibited from taking any separate measures to recover his debt from the Nabob: ... and we further direct, that, if any creditor shall be found refractory, or disposed to disturb the arrangement we have suggested, he shall be dismissed the service, and sent home to England.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make acceptance of the distribution scheme a precondition for receiving any share; forbid separate recovery actions by protected persons and remove/dismiss refractory creditors from Company service.

rubrics_metrics.name: No protection for new or uninvestigated debts owed to British subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: It has been surmised that the Nabob has of late contracted further debts: if any of these are due to British subjects, we forbid any countenance or protection whatever to be given to them, until the debt is fully investigated, the nature of it reported home, and our special instructions upon it received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refuse Company protection to recently alleged debts to British subjects until full local investigation and instructions from home government are obtained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strict prohibition on Company servants engaging in private money transactions with native powers
rubrics_metrics.description: we hereby, in the most pointed and positive terms, repeat our prohibition upon this subject, and direct that no person, being a servant of the Company, or being under our protection, shall, on any pretence whatever, be concerned in any loan or other money transaction with any of the country powers, unless with the knowledge and express permission of our respective governments. And if any of our servants, or others, being under our protection, shall be discovered in any respect counteracting these orders, we strictly enjoin you to take the first opportunity of sending them home to England, to be punished as guilty of disobedience of orders, and no protection or assistance of the Company shall be given for the recovery of any loans connected with such transactions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enforce an absolute ban on private loans/financial dealings between Company servants/protected persons and native rulers without prior written permission; offenders to be sent home and denied Company assistance in recovery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repeat prohibition on intercourse between British subjects and Nabob's family
rubrics_metrics.description: In order to put an end to those intrigues which have been so successfully carried on at the Nabob's durbar, we repeat our prohibition in the strongest terms respecting any intercourse between British subjects and the Nabob and his family;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Curtail private access and influence by British subjects at the Nabob's court to prevent intrigues detrimental to Nabob and public interest; violators to be sent home.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply extra Tanjore peshcush payments to Company's debt when contributed
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Nabob shall be prevailed upon to apply the arrears and growing payments of the Tanjore peshcush in further discharge of his debts, over and above the twelve lacs of pagodas, we direct that the whole of that payment, when made, shall be applied towards the reduction of the Company's debt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When extra Tanjore payments are made, allocate them entirely to reduce Company's outstanding debt as per directions.
